what: TKO Group owns UFC and WWE, the two largest combat sports and sports entertainment properties in the world, plus boxing and event businesses. It makes money mainly by selling media rights to its events.
customers: Broadcasters and streaming services buying rights, live event attendees, sponsors and merchandise buyers.
money: media rights for Raw and SmackDown, live events, premium events
moat: Content people will not watch elsewhere, owned outright rather than licensed from leagues, with a fixed calendar of events that streaming services want to fill schedules.
risks: Revenue fell about 3% last year between rights renewal cycles
It depends on a small number of very large media rights deals
Athlete and talent disputes have led to litigation
opportunities: Revenue grew about 61% a year over three years as UFC and WWE were combined
New media rights deals have repriced its content sharply higher
Analysts see about 25% upside from current levels
watch: Media rights renewals and live event revenue per event.
